items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: It’s like going to the concert hall and listening to Mozart or Chopin or Stravinsky.

ctx.x: I wonder if you landed on something that goes back to what we were talking about as far as America respecting the art form in that what you’re just describing takes some investment from the listener. It’s the fact that there’s no — you know jazz is mostly an instrumental music and people need to be able to use their imagination to enjoy it, and perhaps we’re getting lazy and finding that that’s too much work.

Yeah because jazz is not elevator music. It’s something you have to concentrate when you listen, and you can establish a kind of conversation thing pretending that you will understand what’s going on on stage or in a recording or whatever. You have to pay attention and you have to try to follow what they’re doing and what the artist are sharing with us. And if you don’t do that jazz is — one more time, it’s not elevator music. It’s not a background music. It’s not something that you put there when you’re having…
